title: Understanding Bluff and Fold in Texas Hold'em Poker
summaryJa: ポーカーの「ブラフ」と「フォールド」は基本的な戦術用語です。ブラフは弱いカードを持ちながら強いふりをする行為で、フォールドは自分の手を降りることです。この二つを理解することはテキサスホールデムで成功するために重要です。
segments: In Texas Hold'em poker, a bluff is when a player bets or raises with a weak hand. The player hopes other players will believe he has a strong hand and will fold.
A bluff is a trick. It is not dishonest—it is a normal part of the game.
Let me give you an example of a bluff. You have two cards that are not very good.
The flop comes. The board shows three cards that do not help you.
You are in late position. You decide to make a big bet.
You want other players to think you have a strong hand. If they believe you, they will fold their cards.
Then you win the pot without showing your cards. This is a successful bluff.
Fold is another important term. When you fold, you give up your hand and leave the game.
You put your cards down and do not play anymore in that round. Players fold when they think their hand is not good enough to win.
Folding stops you from losing more money. Here is an example of folding.
You have a weak hand. Your opponent makes a big bet.
You think he has a strong hand. You do not want to lose more money, so you fold.
Your opponent wins the pot. You saved your money by folding early.
Understanding when to bluff and when to fold helps you play better poker.
